scientific_significance.description: A dictionary of affected fields. high means a direct change to core understanding, methods, or capability; medium means clear progress or material downstream impact; low means a local, indirect, or incremental effect. Every entry must concretely say what changes.

solution_difficulty.description: Possible solving obstacles, without a numeric score.

verification_contract.description: Acceptance contracts keyed by answer type. It may be null when a parent delegates verification to subproblems.

ci_contract.description: The part that can run as Continuous Integration: what result is consumed, what is checked, and what makes it pass or fail. Null means no reasonable mechanical check.

verification_difficulty.description: One overall score after mechanically checkable parts of every verification contract have been removed. Scoring procedure: enumerate every accepted answer type; identify CI, formal checking, tests, substitution, finite enumeration, replay, certificates, and other clear mechanical procedures for each type; exclude those parts even when the CI implementation does not yet exist; identify the residual Agent or human Reviewer judgment for each type; then assess all contracts together and assign one score. 0: no residual judgment. 1-3: a few local standard checks. 4-6: connected derivations or substantial problem-answer correspondence work. 7-9: long, fragile, or novel reasoning, or substantial code review. 10: holistic expert judgment. The rationale must explain the mechanical parts, residual judgments, and combined score. This measures review difficulty, not solution difficulty, and is not a gate.
